title: wireformat-microlatency-profile-proto-chunked-draft
body:
Executive summary:
- Purpose: compare wireformat and transport choices for short-lived, interactive sessions (microsessions) where serialization and framing overhead can dominate. We profiled Protocol Buffers (stable, binary) vs chunked JSON (newline-delimited, streaming-friendly) and a small custom compact-json variant used by our edge clients.
- Key finding: for sub-50ms P50 budgets, binary protobuf reduces tail amplification (p90/p99) and CPU serialization time; chunked JSON has lower median for very small payloads when using HTTP/2 multiplexing but suffers at p99 under moderate concurrency due to parse jitter.
- Recommendation (interim): default to protobuf for internal inter-service RPC and the fastpath of private deployments; allow chunked JSON as a developer-friendly opt-in for hosted API streaming where client libs handle incremental parsing.

Test matrix and method:
- Date: runs performed 2028-11-05 through 2028-11-11 on staging infra.
- Targets: inference front proxy -> runtime worker (A100-80GB), colocated with CPU ingress nodes for serialization work.
- Harness: synthetic driver that replays real session traces (sampled from production chat sessions): 3 session types: micro (1-3 turns, median turn tokens 8), short (4-12 turns, median tokens 24), long (20+ turns, median tokens 120).
- Wireformats tested:
  1) protobuf (single-message, binary, zlib disabled)
  2) chunked-json (ndjson framing, chunk size 128B–2KB depending on token emission)
  3) compact-json (custom field name compacting + numeric-only fields encoded as binary blobs)
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32, 128 simultaneous session connections. Each cell is 10-minute steady-state with warmup.
- Measurements: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms) from client-to-first-byte, tokens/sec produced by worker, CPU% on ingress, bytes/request, and an estimate of incremental $/1M requests (token cost excluded — this is framing/transport cost only).

Representative raw table (aggregated averages across session mixes)
Note: columns rounded; cost estimate assumes egress pricing + CPU delta mapped to our rate card.

| Format        | Concurrency | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | tokens/sec | ingress CPU (%) | bytes/req | delta $/1M req |
|---------------|-------------|----------|----------|----------|------------|-----------------|-----------|---------------|
| protobuf      | 1           | 18       | 34       | 68       | 520        | 6               | 420B      | 3.1           |
| protobuf      | 8           | 22       | 45       | 110      | 4,000      | 18              | 420B      | 3.8           |
| protobuf      | 32          | 30       | 88       | 210      | 13,000     | 38              | 420B      | 5.6           |
| protobuf      | 128         | 68       | 180      | 620      | 38,000     | 68              | 420B      | 11.4          |
| chunked-json  | 1           | 16       | 36       | 92       | 540        | 10              | 820B      | 4.5           |
| chunked-json  | 8           | 20       | 70       | 240      | 3,800      | 30              | 820B      | 6.3           |
| chunked-json  | 32          | 42       | 150      | 720      | 12,000     | 64              | 820B      | 13.8          |
| chunked-json  | 128         | 120      | 520      | 2,100    | 35,000     | 92              | 820B      | 28.6          |
| compact-json  | 1           | 20       | 40       | 95       | 510        | 8               | 360B      | 3.4           |
| compact-json  | 8           | 24       | 60       | 150      | 3,900      | 22              | 360B      | 4.5           |
| compact-json  | 32          | 36       | 110      | 360      | 12,500     | 42              | 360B      | 6.9           |
| compact-json  | 128         | 92       | 320      | 1,000    | 36,000     | 76              | 360B      | 16.2          |
\nObservations and interpretation:\n- Median latency: chunked-json slightly wins at concurrency=1 due to lower framing codepath on the client and incremental emit (client perceives first chunk earlier). However, this advantage disappears as concurrency grows.
- Tail latency amplification: chunked-json shows much larger p99 degradation at >=8 concurrent connections, driven by CPU parse jitter and backpressure interactions with the HTTP stack. protobuf remains more stable across p90/p99.
- Bytes/req: chunked-json sends larger wire payloads because NDJSON includes repeated field names and textual tokens; compact-json reduces bytes the most but requires additional encode/decode logic.
- CPU on ingress: parsing chunked JSON is ~1.6x more CPU intensive than binary protobuf for our C++ ingress parser; compact-json sits between them but needs a dedicated deserializer.
- Cost mapping: at larger scales, chunked-json increases infra costs significantly (see delta $/1M req). The 128-concurrency scenario shows a >2x cost vs protobuf primarily from CPU scaling and extra egress.

Session-mix sensitivity:
- Microsessions (1-3 turns): wireformat overhead is proportionally larger. For microsessions, protobuf reduced end-to-end p50 by ~12% compared to chunked-json and cut p99 by ~35%.
- Long sessions: serialization overhead becomes small relative to decode/generation time; all formats converge on tokens/sec. Still, chunked-json increases overall bytes and thus egress cost.

Qualitative notes from logs:
- chunked-json: observed bursts of parse stalls correlated with GC cycles in the node.js front proxy during the 32/128 concurrency sweeps (investigate V8 heap tuning).
- protobuf: occasional 1–2ms jitter tied to buffer copying at edges when using older kernel sendfile fallbacks.
- compact-json: stable but required a small ABI change for client SDK (field name map).

Actionable recommendations (short-term):
1) Default internal fastpath to protobuf for RPC between front proxy and runtime in Dedicated/Private setups.
2) Keep chunked JSON as an opt-in streaming API for hosted customers who prioritize early-first-byte in low-concurrency interactive use; document p99 caveats.
3) Prototype a hybrid: use chunked JSON for initial chunking (first bytes) then switch to protobuf for subsequent frames (experiment in PR #1882).
4) Add ingress-side parse-worker pools for hosted infra to absorb chunked-json CPU spikes (capacity planning ticket ISSUE-3499).

Next experiments (medium-term):
- Repeat runs with zstd compression enabled at various levels to see tradeoffs between bytes/req and CPU parsing cost.
- Profile at the syscall layer to see whether kernel dispatch or userland parsing dominates p99 spikes for chunked-json.
- Test with alternate HTTP stacks (nghttp2 vs custom mux) and with HTTP/3 (QUIC) to measure framing benefits for chunk streaming.

Open questions / unresolved risks:
- How much of chunked-json p99 degradation is attributable to our current Node front-proxy implementation vs the format itself? (Need a clean C++ ingress comparison).
- SDK adoption friction: compact-json requires client updates — what is rollout risk for stable customers?
- Security/cors implications of hybrid wireformat switching (must preserve signing and auth metadata).

Appendix A — short reproducibility notes:
- Harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/wire-bench (branch: proto-chunked-2028)
- Jenkins job: bench-wirereplica-2028-11 (see run ids: 20281105-01..-10)
- Commandline snippet (running single-case):
  ./bench-driver --profile trace-110 --format protobuf --concurrency 32 \\n    --session-sample-file samples/microsessions-2028-10.json \\n    --duration 600 --warmup 60 --target runtime-staging:443

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a draft: numbers are from a limited pool of infra and should be validated in a separate cross-region pass before any customer-facing collateral is published.
- If we lock protobuf as default, add a short doc for SDK authors describing encoding expectations and migration steps.

Prepared by: Maya Chen (eng-console-and-tooling)
Reviewers: Arjun, Samir, Lina.
